questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Briefly explain why an operating system,

(i) Should be the first software to be installed in a computer system. (2 marks)

(ii) Should be able to carry out multitasking. (2 marks)

(iii) Creates virtual memories. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Why the operating system is installed first (2 marks).** The operating system (OS) manages the hardware (processor, memory, disks, keyboard, screen, printer) and provides the platform on which all the other software works. Application programs and drivers need the OS to run and to use the hardware, so they cannot be installed or run until an OS is present. The OS is also the program loaded at start-up that makes the computer usable.

**(ii) Why it should carry out multitasking (2 marks).** Users want to run several programs at the same time (for example a word processor, a music player and a web browser). The OS shares the processor time between the programs very quickly (scheduling) and shares the memory between them, so that all the programs seem to run together, which saves time and uses the processor efficiently, because the processor does not stay idle while a program waits for input or output.

**(iii) Why it creates virtual memory (2 marks).** The main memory (RAM) is limited. When RAM is full the OS uses part of the hard disk as an extension of RAM (swap or paging file) and moves the parts of programs that are not in use to it. This makes it possible to run big programs, or many programs at the same time, that would not fit in RAM alone.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Identify and briefly describe the role of any five (05) basic hardware components (or devices) that are involved from the moment data is input to a computer system until, when a hardcopy is generated from the system. (10 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Five hardware components, in the order the data passes through them (10 marks: 1 mark to identify and 1 mark for the role, for each component)**

1. **Input device, for example the keyboard (or mouse, scanner):** used to enter data and instructions into the computer.
2. **Central processing unit (CPU):** the "brain" of the computer; its control unit fetches and decodes the instructions and its arithmetic and logic unit processes the data.
3. **Main memory (RAM):** holds temporarily the data and the instructions that the CPU is working on.
4. **Secondary storage device, for example the hard disk:** stores programs and data permanently, so that they are kept when the computer is switched off.
5. **Output device that produces the hardcopy: the printer:** prints the result of the processing on paper (a hardcopy). (The monitor, also an output device, gives a softcopy.)

Any five correct components with their roles are accepted.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Convert each of the following showing clear working,

(i) The hexadecimal (base 16) number $B2A_{16}$ to Binary (base 2). (2 marks)

(ii) The octal (base 8) number $6257_8$ to Hexadecimal (base 16). (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) $B2A_{16}$ to binary (2 marks).** Each hexadecimal digit is replaced by its 4-bit binary group:

| Hex digit | B | 2 | A |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decimal value | 11 | 2 | 10 |
| Binary | 1011 | 0010 | 1010 |

$B2A_{16} = 1011\,0010\,1010_2$

**(ii) $6257_8$ to hexadecimal (2 marks).** Step 1: each octal digit is replaced by its 3-bit binary group.

| Octal digit | 6 | 2 | 5 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Binary | 110 | 010 | 101 | 111 |

So $6257_8 = 110\,010\,101\,111_2$.

Step 2: regroup the bits in fours from the right: $1100\ 1010\ 1111$, that is $C$, $A$, $F$ (since $1100 = 12 = C$, $1010 = 10 = A$, $1111 = 15 = F$).

$6257_8 = CAF_{16}$

Check: $6257_8 = 6 \times 512 + 2 \times 64 + 5 \times 8 + 7 = 3247$ and $CAF_{16} = 12 \times 256 + 10 \times 16 + 15 = 3247$.
